findings.claim: The attribute is wrapped in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`, so consumers targeting netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework get no `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage` on any generated formatter or resolver. The requirement asks for all generated code to be decorated. `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` already exists on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework 4.0+ and applies to classes, so the exclusion is not needed for compilation. It silently drops the feature for a large share of supported targets.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageDownlevelTests.GeneratedTypesKeepAttributeWhenDownlevelSymbolDefined (both InlineData cases). It runs the generator with NETSTANDARD2_0 or NETFRAMEWORK defined and asserts every generated formatter/resolver class symbol carries ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute. On head the attribute is preprocessed out and the test fails. The same `#if` appears in EnumTemplate.tt, UnionTemplate.tt, StringKeyFormatterTemplate.tt, ResolverTemplate.tt and CompositeResolverTemplate.tt.

findings.claim: The README says the attribute 'is only emitted for targets where it is available (not netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework)'. That is factually wrong, because ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute is available on both. It documents the target gap as a platform limitation instead of a choice.

receipt_plan.detail: Compare README.md:1640 with the netstandard2.0 / net462 reference assemblies: System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute is present in netstandard.dll (2.0) and in mscorlib/System.dll (4.0+).

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Unconditional, no setting: every template (formatter, string-key formatter, enum, union, resolver, composite resolver, and their FormatterCache/GetFormatterHelper nested classes) always emits [global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]. Users have no way to turn it off. This is what the change implements, apart from its target-framework #if.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Emitted by default with an opt-out setting. Add a boolean option to GeneratorOptions/FormatterOptions, for example an `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage` property on the [GeneratedMessagePackResolver] attribute or an MSBuild/analyzer-config property, defaulting to true. Thread it into each template as `<# if (Options.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage) { #>` around the attribute lines, and document the setting in README.
